Role and Responsibilities Develop and implement a comprehensive information security strategy that aligns with the organization’s goals while ensuring compliance with public healthcare IT security policies and standards. Ability to translate complex cyber and technology risks into clear business, clinical, and service impact narratives for senior leadership and Boards. Strong knowledge of information security frameworks, risk management and compliance requirements. Proficiency in security technologies and tools. Ability to engage confidently with senior stakeholders and translate technical risks into actionable business recommendations. jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Carbon Strategy Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Jul 2026. Closing on 31 Aug 2026. Would you like to play a role in charting the path forward for Singapore’s low-carbon transition? This is the key responsibility of the Carbon Strategy Division within MTI’s Energy and Carbon cluster. Making the transition to a low-carbon economy in a secure and cost-competitive manner is critical for Singapore. With finite resources and an open economy, Singapore faces unique trade-offs and challenges in making this transition, requiring innovation in technology and policy to seize new opportunities in a carbon-constrained world. MTI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships. The Carbon Strategy Division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in cross-cutting policymaking to decarbonise our economy and meet our Net Zero targets, while maintaining our economic competitiveness. We are looking for driven and capable officers who (i) thrive in a fast-moving environment, (ii) have a keen interest in carbon, energy and economic transition policy, and (iii) are adept at working with multiple stakeholders within and outside the public sector. In particular, the officer will be responsible for one or more of the following workstreams: (a) Developing strategies for national mitigation measures, leveraging carbon tax implementation and the deployment of the Carbon Mitigation Programme Budget; (b) Leading the development of industry decarbonisation policies, through the development of effective incentive schemes and other levers; (c) Overseeing R&D efforts into longer-term industry decarbonisation pathways. The candidate should be equipped with the following competencies: • Possess strong analytical skills, and be able to provide policy recommendations by drawing on a wide variety of sources; • Have a keen interest in the development and deployment of policies and technologies that can support Singapore’s Net Zero ambitions; • Be very comfortable working with a wide range of stakeholders, both within and beyond the public service, which requires strong interpersonal, organisational and communication skills; • Possess the ability to work well both independently and as part of a team; • Be driven, meticulous and resourceful; • Candidates with relevant experience in policy-related work (particularly in the public sector), and sustainability and energy-related fields will be assessed favourably.

Hence, we have to work together with the international community to address climate change and build a climate resilient future. The transition to a low-carbon and green economy will be especially challenging for Singapore, given our scarce natural resources and open economy. jobs.title: Asst Director/Snr Asst Director/Deputy Director (Medical Service Scheme)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 5 Aug 2026. Closing on 31 Dec 2026. Shape Singapore’s Health at the National Level Are you a medical doctor looking to make an impact beyond a clinical setting? Whether you are a junior doctor exploring your career options, or an established clinician contemplating new challenges to contribute at the national level, consider a career at the Ministry of Health (MOH). Under the MOH Medical Service Scheme employment, you will bring your clinical lens and expertise to national healthcare policies and influence decisions that shape the health of Singapore. You will work at the intersection of medicine and policy to design the healthcare systems and frameworks that aim to improve the health outcomes for the nation, and be part of the national health leadership. You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. This is a role for doctors who are energised by complexity, motivated by purpose, and ready to drive healthcare transformation at a national scale. You will contribute across four key domain areas: • Healthcare Regulation — Safeguarding standards and ensuring the safety, quality, and integrity of Singapore's healthcare system. • Manpower Development & Capability Building — Shaping the pipeline and professional development of Singapore's healthcare workforce. • Population Health & Health Services — Designing and delivering health programmes and services that keep Singaporeans healthy across their life course. • Quality, Value & Informatics — Driving innovation, data-driven decision making, and value in healthcare delivery. At more senior levels, you may also lead and manage a team. As part of your development, you may also be rotated to other public sector agencies and organisations within the broader healthcare ecosystem — such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Health Promotion Board (HPB), Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA), or the public healthcare clusters. Your postings will be carefully designed to broaden your exposure and deepen your understanding of how policy translates into operations on the ground, equipping you with a well-rounded perspective to grow and contribute meaningfully throughout your career with MOH. While you will mostly be involved in healthcare policy work, you may also continue with sessional clinical practice, if you prefer, at the public healthcare institutions, so that you can maintain your clinical currency and familiarity with ground operations. We welcome applications from medical doctors who are registered with the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) and remain in good standing. Beyond your medical qualifications, we are looking for doctors who embody the following: • Collaborative Spirit: You work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and are energised by cross-agency initiatives that drive system-wide change. • Critical Thinking: You bring your medical perspectives to bear on complex policy questions, evaluating evidence rigorously to inform national healthcare decisions. • Capacity for Change: You are adaptable and responsive to evolving health priorities, emerging challenges, and shifting policy landscapes. • Commitment to Continuous Learning: You are passionate about growing beyond clinical practice — into the domains of healthcare policy, regulation, and population health strategy. • Compassion: You connect with diverse stakeholders with empathy, and understand how policy decisions translate into real outcomes for real people. We are also looking for doctors who demonstrate strength in systems thinking — the ability to understand complex healthcare ecosystems as a whole— as well as strategic thinking and the leadership capacity to inspire and guide teams through transformation. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, applicants may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Low-Carbon Energy Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 9 Jul 2026. Closing on 31 Aug 2026. Energy security is an existential issue for Singapore. At the same time, geopolitical pressures are causing significant stresses in energy markets, leading to risks of supply disruptions and significant price volatility. The energy transition will be especially challenging for Singapore, given our scarce natural resources and limited renewable energy options. One of Singapore’s biggest challenges over the next few decades is to secure a low-carbon energy supply that is reliable and cost-competitive. The future of Singapore’s energy landscape depends on our ability to harness four switches – natural gas, solar, electricity imports, and low-carbon solutions such as hydrogen, ammonia and carbon capture and storage. MTI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships. The Low-Carbon Energy division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in: • Developing, implementing and monitoring various alternative energy sources for Singapore, including solar, hydrogen in its various forms, bioenergy, geothermal energy, as well as other promising low-carbon technologies. • Devising new policies to ensure that new energy solutions can be productively deployed and scaled sufficiently to help meet our 2050 net zero goals. • Overseeing issues relating to energy, grid, storage and carbon transformation Research & Development in Singapore. This could also entail the development of new climate technology pilot funding scheme, working directly with global climate tech solution providers, academics, and investors. Your responsibilities may include one or more of the following workstreams: • Develop strategies and policies to support the implementation of the Singapore National Hydrogen Strategy (published in October 2022), with a focus on: - Development of commercial industry projects to develop hydrogen supply chains in Singapore - Long-term infrastructure and land planning - Competitive monitoring - Advancement of international collaboration to leverage like-minded partners’ efforts to advance regional hydrogen supply chains and interoperable standards and regulations - Facilitate collaborations across key stakeholders, involving Government agencies, industry players, academia and international counterparts as appropriate • Develop and implement R&D strategies in areas that are critical to Singapore’s energy interests and supports the development of Singapore enterprise • Engage with new energy and decarbonization-focused companies and funds to track, monitor and make relevant recommendations with regards to the latest developments in the climate technology realm • Develop and implement communications and engagement plans with regard to Singapore’s alternative energy policies • Monitor developments in global energy landscape and analyse implications for domestic energy policies to enable these developments We are looking for matured, driven, self-aware, coachable and capable individuals who possess a strong desire to contribute and directly enable Singapore’s energy transition, thrive in a fast-moving environment across organisational boundaries and geographies, have a strong interest in alternative energy technologies and policies, and are equipped with the following qualities and competencies: •

jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Jul 2026. Closing on 31 Aug 2026. MTI’s Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division plays a key role in ensuring Singapore’s energy security and creating an energy system that is resilient, cost-competitive, and ready to transition to a low carbon future. Energy security is an existential issue for Singapore. We import almost all our energy supply and are exposed to global energy market movements. The energy crisis after COVID and the war in Ukraine have upended the global energy ecosystem. The climate crisis compels all countries to accelerate their pace of decarbonisation, even as they struggle with energy costs and unpredictable supply chain shocks. Amidst this backdrop, Singapore needs a stable, reliable, and cost competitive energy system that keeps the lights on and safeguards our economic competitiveness and dynamism. MTI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships. The Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in: • Planning for Singapore’s energy transition and resilience, including energy demand and supply and the corresponding impact on infrastructure requirements, system costs and electricity prices. • Strengthening Singapore’s gas and electricity markets and our national grid infrastructure • Developing horizontal enablers for the energy sector e.g. manpower and skills development, energy public engagement strategy. jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Energy Partnerships Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Jul 2026. Closing on 31 Aug 2026. By joining the Energy Partnerships Division at MTI, you will become part of a critical and urgent mission: to support Singapore’s energy transition by securing low-carbon electricity imports from our region and building an interconnected regional grid. Low-carbon electricity imports are one of Singapore’s ‘Four Switches’, alongside natural gas, solar, and low-carbon solutions such as hydrogen, ammonia, and carbon capture and storage. The climate crisis requires us to quickly transition to low-carbon energy sources to avoid the devastating impact of rising temperatures. Decarbonising our power sector, which contributes 40% of current emissions, is key to realising Singapore’s commitment to achieving net zero emissions by 2050. Even as we take steps to secure a low-carbon energy supply, we will also need to safeguard our energy security and affordability. Navigating the energy trilemma successfully will be one of the defining policy challenges of our generation and hold far-reaching implications for our economy and society. In 2027, Singapore will take on the ASEAN Chairmanship. For the energy sectoral track, this will be an important opportunity to advance regional cooperation and drive progress on energy connectivity through the ASEAN Power Grid (APG). MTI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships. The Energy Partnerships Division within the E&C cluster formulates Singapore’s energy policies and strategies, together with the Energy Market Authority, other Government agencies, academics, and private sector stakeholders. The Energy Partnerships Division takes the lead in: • Driving Singapore’s efforts to import and deploy renewable energy from the region to realise target to import around 6GW of low-carbon electricity by 2035 to decarbonise our power system. • Advancing energy collaboration with like-minded countries, international organisations, and think tanks to support Singapore and the region’s energy transition and energy resilience, and advocate for the APG. Your responsibilities include one or more of the following workstreams: • Drive G2G engagements, including through visits, working groups, dialogues, and instruments of collaboration such as agreements and memoranda of understanding, to advance the realisation of cross-border electricity trading projects. • Develop policies and strategies to advance the financing of cross-border power transmission infrastructure; the manufacturing, deployment and protection of subsea power cables; and the recognition of cross-border Renewable Energy Certificates to support the implementation of cross-border electricity imports projects. • Develop and strengthen partnerships with international thought leaders such as the International Energy Agency (IEA), International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), Multilateral Development Banks, as well as local partners such as the Energy Studies Institute and Asia Competitiveness Institute. • Foster collaborations with like-minded partners at: (1) Local events such as Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) (2) Multilateral international platforms such as ASEAN Ministers on Energy Meeting (AMEM), G20, and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC). It helps HPB clarify whether an opportunity should proceed, stop, pivot, transition to a business unit, scale further, or be translated into useful insights for wider organisational learning. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 Jul 2026. Closing on 12 Aug 2026. The Maintenance Enforcement Division (“MED”) is a new division under the Insolvency and Public Trustee’s Office (“IPTO”). The MED enhances access to justice by improving the process for enforcing maintenance arrears. A summary of the maintenance enforcement process and the role of the MEO can be found in this video (https://med.mlaw.gov.sg/video-role-of-maintenanance-enforcement-officers/). Your responsibilities as a Maintenance Enforcement Officer (MEO) in the MED will include the following: a) Managing your own cases relating to the enforcement of maintenance orders. You will conduct (1) fact-finding and (2) conciliation, and (3) write reports regarding your findings. In conciliation, which replaces the existing mediation process, MEOs will play a more active role in seeking information and recommending solutions to the parties. You will be required to understand agreements reached between parties and draft the corresponding Consent Order. You will also need to appear in court via video-conferencing to assist parties in recording the Consent Order. You may also be required to appear in court if the judge requires your attendance to address any queries regarding the report. b) Beyond your casework, you will also have the opportunity to contribute to projects relating to, amongst others, enhancing operational workflows, developing IT systems and testing GenAI products, and evaluating the maintenance enforcement process. Key competencies a) [Strong interpersonal and communication skills] Strong communication abilities and emotional resilience to manage hostile or emotional situations, de-escalate conflicts, and facilitate constructive dialogue between parties with fundamental disagreements, particularly drawing from family law work, social work or counselling experience. b) [Investigating and Gathering Evidence] Ensure all evidence related to the case are appropriately obtained, documented, processed, and stored in accordance with agency policy and procedures to support case resolution. Able to assess financial information and formulate practical settlement proposals based on parties’ financial circumstances and needs (including understanding of common financial documents such as bank, CPF, and IRAS statements as well as payslips) c) [Case management] Independently manage multiple case files progression, as well as related financial matters while ensuring compliance with SOP and timelines. d) [Leveraging on technology] Keep up to date on technological trends relevant to my work in enforcement, and adopt relevant technology-enabled solutions to address current and future enforcement challenges. e) [Application of law] Demonstrate understanding of and apply the fundamental legal principles, laws, legislation and government regulation to the relevant areas of work. f) [Litigation support] Prepare high quality and accurate written correspondence as well as court papers such as the MEO Report or follow-up reports to be submitted to the Court within required timeline. g) [Data Analytics] Proficiency in data analysis with strong Microsoft Excel skills, including advanced functions, pivot tables, and data visualisation, experience in interpreting datasets and translating findings into actionable insights. Personal traits Candidates should: a) Possess strong verbal and written communication skills b) Be able to do front-line work with members of public c) Have a keen interest in the development of ops-policies and operational work d) Be meticulous and capable of collecting and evaluating complex or multifaceted information e) Prior experience in mediation, legal drafting, handling casework that involves family disputes, family law practice, finance, accounting will be an advantage, but is not a pre-requisite for the role. f) Ability to speak local languages/dialects will be an advantage.

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 24 Jul 2026. Closing in 2 day(s). You will formulate, assess and review strategies, policies and programmes to achieve MDDI’s vision of a safe and inclusive Digital Society, where Singaporeans are empowered to harness opportunities afforded by digital technologies, and able to thrive in a digital future. Key policy domains include digital access; inclusive digital design; digital skills, literacy and future readiness; digital well-being, citizenry, and safety. As Assistant Director, you will be expected to lead a small team to deliver on projects / a workstream. • Contribute to the division’s efforts to develop, drive, coordinate and review digital readiness policies, strategies and programmes for individuals and micro-enterprises across MDDI, its agencies (i.e. the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), the National Library Board (NLB), the Cyber Security Agency (CSA), the Government Technology Agency (GovTech)) and across the Whole of Government (WOG), working closely with relevant ministries and agencies. • Contribute to the coordination and driving a whole-of-MDDI approach and strategy for public education efforts and ensure that approach is relevant, cohesive and effective in addressing emerging issues. This includes planning, formulating and coordinating public communications approaches to engage Singaporeans. • Develop and maintain an extensive network of relationships across public, private and people sectors, and ensure an effective and meaningful way to engage, galvanise and bring onboard partners and volunteers to contribute to enhancing the quality, reach and impact of policies and programmes. • Commission research studies, conduct environment scans and collaborate with local and overseas academia and think tanks to enhance understanding of international and local developments to ensure currency of our efforts and ensure desired outcomes are achieved. This includes working with MDDI divisions to coordinate research agenda and to propagate research outcomes across Whole of Government (WOG) where relevant. • Contribute to the development and implementation of tools and approaches for the measurement and assessment of Digital Society outcomes in Singapore • Contribute to WOG agenda for lifelong learning through the review and formulation of policies, strategies and programmes related to libraries, archives and learning. • Provide secretariat work for committees and structures that will drive the above. • Excellent writing and communication skills • Strong ability to analyse and think critically about complex issues • Background in any relevant discipline (e.g. social sciences, communications) • Passionate about the promotion of digital inclusion, digital literacy, digital well-being and lifelong learning • Team player with excellent interpersonal skills and good stakeholder management skills • Work experience in public sector or social services agencies would be advantageous We regret to inform that only shortlisted candidates would be notified. For more information on careers in MDDI, please access the link (https://www.mddi.gov.sg/join-us/careers/life-at-mddi/). For more information on our job vacancies, please access Careers@Gov (https://www.careers.gov.sg/) and search for “MDDI” in the Search bar.

jobs.title: Senior Executive / Assistant Director (Compliance & Professional Standards)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 12 Sep 2025. Closing on 15 Aug 2026. jobs.title: Assistant Director/Senior Assistant Director, Land Policy Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 7 Jun 2026. Closing on 31 Aug 2026. As an Assistant Director / Senior Assistant Director in the Land Policy Division in the Ministry of Law, you will drive the development and review of legislation, policies, and strategies, to optimise land use for Singapore’s social and economic development. The key policy areas which you may be involved in include: (a) Optimisation and Management of State land and properties (b) Land Sales and Lease Administration (c) Acquisition and safeguarding of land for public purposes (d) Property registration and Collective Sales (e) Safeguarding of residential land You will be involved in the entire policy formulation process and conduct analysis of the policy issues; engage relevant Government agencies, stakeholders, and industry players, to gather feedback and get buy-in; prepare papers and submissions to seek approval for your proposals; and work with stakeholders to implement the policy changes. jobs.title: Assistant Director / Senior Manager (Sector Development)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 31 Oct 2025. Closing on 12 Aug 2026. You will play a key role in (i) fostering partnerships through account management of key aviation stakeholders; (ii) formulating and implementing industry development policies with a focus on the air cargo and ground handling sectors, and (iii) developing and evaluating grant proposals from aviation companies to support their capacity development and service innovation. This will involve developing long-term policies to support the air hub’s growth, particularly in the transformation of airport operations and in air cargo. You will craft policy papers and presentations to substantiate the policy direction and strategies CAAS is taking to drive industry transformation. In addition, you will account manage key stakeholders in the air transport sector, supporting their enterprise development plans and efforts. This would include partnering companies in developing and implementing innovative solutions to enhance passenger experience and airport operations through automation and digitalisation, and to administer grants awarded by CAAS to catalyse and accelerate such projects. You will also work closely with relevant Divisions and colleagues within CAAS to track and monitor the impact of innovation and productivity efforts and grants to ensure the sector is future-ready and resilient, as well as external government partners such as EDB and JTC. Training in any discipline, preferably Business, Economics, or other relevant disciplines Minimum 5 years working experience with 2-3 years in public policy, preferably in industry development or account management Independent and resourceful self-starter, with drive and initiative and able to engage wide variety of stakeholders independently to identify new opportunities for partnership Strong writing and presentation skills, with the ability to convey your views clearly and succinctly Strong team player, with the ability to work closely with multiple stakeholders across both public and private sector agencies Meticulous, self-motivated and resourceful Note: Your appointment designation will be commensurate with your relevant work experience. jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director (Policy Design & Programme Evaluation), Economics Div
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 May 2026. Policy design and programme evaluation is the systematic analysis of policies, programmes and schemes to assess their impact, effectiveness and efficiency. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 14 Jul 2026. Closing on 14 Aug 2026. jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Supply Chain and Economic Resilience Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 5 Jun 2026. Closing on 30 Sep 2026. With the shifts in the global order and deepening geopolitical tensions, we live in a world which is less predictable and secure. In recent years, global supply chains are increasingly being scrutinised for their ability to withstand shocks. Countries are reconfiguring trade networks and supply chains in the name of resilience and security. As a small and open economy with limited natural resources, Singapore needs to be prepared and reacts nimbly in the face of such changes . The Supply Chain and Economic Resilience Division (SCERD) is responsible for ensuring economic resilience and the resilience of Singapore’s critical supply chains. SCERD also oversees building and institutionalising resilience, operational preparedness and crisis management capabilities in the Ministry of Trade and Industry. In this role, you will: • Develop national and sectoral strategies to secure the resilience of Singapore’s supply chains for essential and critical goods and services, and to mitigate and withstand impact from external shocks; • Analyse and synthesize findings on critical sector supply chains, challenges and needs; • Build the division’s collaboration network with key stakeholders across the Government, industry and academia; • Strengthen supply chain intelligence and analysis capabilities. Requirements • Excellent writing, communication, interpersonal and presentation skills; • Able to work independently as well as in teams, and across multiple workstreams; • Aptitude for policy design, systems and analytical thinking, in order to deal with complex problems and recommend actionable solutions; • Possess a driven and self-starter attitude as well as resourcefulness in solving problems; • Good stakeholder management skills dealing both with internal and external stakeholders; and • Data analysis skills including data visualisation and the ability to extract insights from complex datasets.

jobs.title: Assistant Director (Family Intervention), RSM/FI
jobs.inst: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 31 Jul 2026. Closing on 13 Aug 2026. Rehabilitation & Social Mobility (RSM) Policy Directorate develops policies and programmes which: a) Deliver stability, self-reliance and social mobility for lower income families b) Protect individuals and families from abuse and neglect or problem gambling c) Rehabilitate individuals from social dysfunction. Family Intervention Division develop and review policies which enhance intervention, stability and resilience of youth-at-risk and vulnerable families (including those with problem gamblers). You will be part of a team of officers who will be working with other Ministries and Divisions within MSF and our stakeholders to formulate and conceptualise comprehensive family service policies and programmes. In particular, your work on family services targeting moderate-to-high-risk vulnerable families and individuals will focus on designing systems and policies that intervene upstream and downstream to influence family functioning, reduce risk and strengthen protective factors. Your responsibilities as a Assistant Director (Family Intervention) will include: • Collaborate with external stakeholders and partners across Ministries and Divisions to formulate, implement and evaluate family service policies targeting moderate-to-high-risk vulnerable families. • Work closely with policy, operations and practice divisions within MSF to ensure seamless integration between policy development, service delivery and frontline practice, facilitating regular coordination and alignment across different functional areas. • Conceptualise and design upstream and downstream intervention systems that influence family functioning, reduce risk factors and strengthen protective factors. • Conduct policy research and analysis to inform evidence-based approaches to family service delivery and intervention strategies. • Plan and carry out stakeholder engagement activities with partners, service providers and other stakeholders/beneficiary groups to ensure responsive policy development. • Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of family service policies and programmes, using data analysis to inform continuous improvement and refinement. • [If given supervisory responsibilities] Lead a team of officers to carry out the above responsibilities. Competencies required: • [Policy Development & Analysis] Formulate comprehensive policies by analysing complex social issues, evaluating evidence, and developing frameworks that address the needs of vulnerable families while considering implementation feasibility. • [Cross-Agency Collaboration] Build and maintain effective partnerships across government divisions, external agencies and community stakeholders to ensure coordinated policy development and service delivery. • [Programme Design & Implementation] Conceptualise and design family service programmes from inception to implementation, ensuring alignment between policy objectives and operational delivery mechanisms. • [Stakeholder Engagement] Develop and execute engagement strategies with families, service providers, and community partners to inform policy development and ensure responsive service design. Requirements: To be successful in this role, you must have/be: • Possess excellent written skills and verbal skills to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders • Strong project management abilities with experience in managing complex timelines and coordinating multi-stakeholder initiatives • Strong collaborative skills and teams ethos to work effectively across multiple divisions • Ability to translate complex policy concepts and research findings into accessible language/non-technical jargon for diverse audience • Interest or experience in social policy development or related fields (3 – 5 years’ experience) would be advantageous • Knowledge of family systems theory, risk assessment frameworks and intervention approaches would be advantageous

jobs.title: Programme Head (Digital Engagement & Adoption)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 17 Feb 2026. Closing on 17 Sep 2026. IMDA’s vision is to build a dynamic digital economy, and a cohesive digital society, driven by an exceptional Infocomm and media ecosystem. jobs.title: Senior Executive / Assistant Director (Maintenance Enforcement Division)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 27 Dec 2024. Closing on 18 Aug 2026. The Maintenance Enforcement Division (“MED”) is a new division under the Insolvency and Public Trustee’s Office (“IPTO”). The MED enhances access to justice by improving the process for enforcing maintenance arrears. A summary of the maintenance enforcement process and the role of the MEO can be found in this video (https://med.mlaw.gov.sg/video-role-of-maintenanance-enforcement-officers/). Your responsibilities as a Maintenance Enforcement Officer (MEO) in the MED will include the following: a) Managing your own cases relating to the enforcement of maintenance orders. You will conduct (1) fact-finding and (2) conciliation, and (3) write reports regarding your findings. In conciliation, which replaces the existing mediation process, MEOs will play a more active role in seeking information and recommending solutions to the parties. You will be required to understand agreements reached between parties and draft the corresponding Consent Order. You will also need to appear in court via video-conferencing to assist parties in recording the Consent Order. You may also be required to appear in court if the judge requires your attendance to address any queries regarding the report. b) Beyond your casework, you will also have the opportunity to contribute to projects relating to, amongst others, enhancing operational workflows, developing IT systems and testing GenAI products, and evaluating the maintenance enforcement process. Key competencies a) [Strong interpersonal and communication skills] Strong communication abilities and emotional resilience to manage hostile or emotional situations, de-escalate conflicts, and facilitate constructive dialogue between parties with fundamental disagreements, particularly drawing from family law work, social work or counselling experience. b) [Investigating and Gathering Evidence] Ensure all evidence related to the case are appropriately obtained, documented, processed, and stored in accordance with agency policy and procedures to support case resolution. Able to assess financial information and formulate practical settlement proposals based on parties’ financial circumstances and needs (including understanding of common financial documents such as bank, CPF, and IRAS statements as well as payslips) c) [Case management] Independently manage multiple case files progression, as well as related financial matters while ensuring compliance with SOP and timelines. d) [Leveraging on technology] Keep up to date on technological trends relevant to my work in enforcement, and adopt relevant technology-enabled solutions to address current and future enforcement challenges. e) [Application of law] Demonstrate understanding of and apply the fundamental legal principles, laws, legislation and government regulation to the relevant areas of work. f) [Litigation support] Prepare high quality and accurate written correspondence as well as court papers such as the MEO Report or follow-up reports to be submitted to the Court within required timeline. g) [Data Analytics] Proficiency in data analysis with strong Microsoft Excel skills, including advanced functions, pivot tables, and data visualisation, experience in interpreting datasets and translating findings into actionable insights. Personal traits Candidates should: a) Possess strong verbal and written communication skills b) Be able to do front-line work with members of public c) Have a keen interest in the development of ops-policies and operational work d) Be meticulous and capable of collecting and evaluating complex or multifaceted information e) Prior experience in mediation, legal drafting, handling casework that involves family disputes, family law practice, finance, accounting will be an advantage, but is not a pre-requisite for the role. f) Ability to speak local languages/dialects will be an advantage.

jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, International Trade (GES)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 May 2026. The Trade and International Economic Relations (TIER) cluster drives the formulation of Singapore's foreign economic policy and advances Singapore's economic interests in the international economic arena. Climate change is one of the defining issues of our time. It is a complex global challenge that calls for concerted international action and collaboration between governments, industry and individuals. As a low-lying city state, Singapore is particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change and has a strong interest in shaping effective global climate action. The Green Economy and Sustainability (GES) team sits within MTI’s International Trade Division, which is charged with formulating Singapore’s foreign economic policy and advancing Singapore’s economic interests in the internationally. The GES team leads Singapore’s international economic engagement on green trade issues. We also work closely with agencies, such as MSE, MOF, NEA and PMO(NCCS), to formulate and coordinate strategies to chart the path forward for Singapore’s transition to a low-carbon economy. As a TIER officer in the International Trade (GES) Division in the Ministry of Trade and Industry, you will be part of a high-performing team operating at the forefront of international economic diplomacy and climate policy, shaping the rules and frameworks that will define the global green economy. You will work on one or more of the following work streams: a. Negotiation of Article 6.2 bilateral/plurilateral agreements. Develop and implement strategies and policies to strengthen bilateral cooperation with like-minded countries on carbon credits aligned with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. Officer will negotiate binding bilateral and plurilateral agreements with foreign governments, drive technical cooperation initiatives, and build robust project development pipelines — directly contributing to Singapore's ability to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). b. Global carbon market rules and standards setting. Monitor and analyse evolving global carbon market developments and develop strategies to actively shape the international rules and standards that govern high-integrity carbon markets, positioning Singapore as a credible and influential voice in this space. c. Green trade policy development. Synthesise geopolitical, trade, and climate trends to craft Singapore's green trade policy agenda, safeguarding the country's long-term economic competitiveness through the low-carbon transition. The officer’s work will directly inform how Singapore positions itself in an increasingly climate-conscious global trading environment. d. Green trade instruments negotiation. Negotiate international instruments across multilateral, plurilateral, and bilateral fronts to advance Singapore's green trade interests. Officer will work with Ministries across the government to tackle complex, cross-cutting issues spanning environmental goods, services and investments, trade-related climate measures (TrCMs), environmental attribute certificates (EACs), and sectoral areas such as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and green buildings. e. Multilateral negotiations. Represent Singapore at the highest levels of international climate diplomacy, including at the UNFCCC Conference of the Parties (COP). You will advocate for Singapore's green economy and low-carbon interests, building coalitions and influencing outcomes that have real-world consequences for global climate action. As the climate space is fast evolving, an officer may be deployed across different workstreams, based on the officer’s development and MTI’s organisational needs. • Experience in cross-cultural negotiations and international relations, particularly in the public sector; and/or • Good knowledge in carbon credits/markets and Paris Agreement; and/or • Good knowledge of green trade related issues including trade-related climate measures, environmental attributes certifications and se

jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, ASEAN Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 May 2026. The Trade and International Economic Relations (TIER) cluster drives the formulation of Singapore's foreign economic policy and advances Singapore's economic interests in the international economic arena. To enable our businesses and jobholders to seize these opportunities, MTI’s ASEAN Division advances Singapore’s economic interests and deepens regional economic integration at the ASEAN platform. Specifically, we seek to boost flows of goods, services, investments, data, people and ideas to strengthen the broader regional economic ecosystem. jobs.title: SENIOR EXECUTIVE/ ASSISTANT DIRECTOR, ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY DIVISION
jobs.inst: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 May 2026. Closing in 6 day(s). At MSE and our family of agencies – PUB, NEA, and SFA – we drive sustainability and resilience initiatives that improve the everyday lives of Singaporeans. As part of the MSE Family, you will be at the forefront of innovation, leading efforts to safeguard water resources, protect public health, and ensure food safety. Through partnerships across sectors, we tackle evolving challenges while fostering an inclusive, safe, and supportive workplace. Join us in shaping Singapore’s sustainable future and making a lasting impact on the everyday lives of generations to come. Environmental sustainability has underpinned Singapore’s policymaking since our independence. As a small city state with limited natural resources, we had to protect our environment to preserve our longer-term developmental opportunities. As early as the 1970s, we started putting in place policies to do so by managing pollution and conserving our water resources. Today, Singapore is widely recognised as a green and sustainable city, and Singaporeans enjoy clean air, water and environment. Environment sustainability remains a key priority for the government. The Environmental Policy Division evaluates, reviews and formulates environmental and sustainability policies and strategies. This spans a broad range of areas including Environmental Public Health, Hawker Centres and Markets, Environmental Protection, as well as Zero Waste and Circular Economy. We are looking for a Senior Executive/ Assistant Director to be part of the Environmental Public Health Policy team. Environmental public health affects all of us every day – whether we notice it or not. It is a dynamic, multi-disciplinary field that spans across policies on public cleanliness, indoor air quality, second-hand smoke exposure, vector control, and after-death facilities and services. As Singapore’s urban and dense setting poses unique challenges to environmental public health, there is a need to push the boundaries of innovative policymaking so that we can harness technology, shape public behaviour, and navigate complex trade-offs to ensure that Singapore remains clean, green, and a liveable home for everyone. As part of the Environmental Policy Division, you will play an important role in shaping policies that make a tangible difference to environmental public health. In the role, you will have the opportunity to: • Gain exposure and build expertise in a wide range of topics, including public cleanliness, indoor air quality, second-hand smoke exposure, vector control, and after-death facilities and services • Drive and formulate strategic policies and programmes to advance policy objectives in environmental public health and environmental sustainability • Perform research and analysis on environmental public health policies to evaluate and guide policy and programme design and implementation • Review policies and legislation to ensure that policies are effective and continue to meet evolving policy objectives and operational requirements You will also have the opportunity to contribute to forward-looking projects on environmental sustainability within the Environment Policy Division. • Strong analytical and synthesis skills. • Able to handle complexity and ambiguity, while remaining grounded in logical and creative problem-solving. • Strong communication skills, both in writing and speaking. • Strong interpersonal, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills. • Ability to drive deliverables independently and in teams. • Have a passion for and openness to learn. • Keen interest in environmental sustainability and willingness to explore different policy areas. Prior experience in policy development will be an advantage, but not a necessity.

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Jun 2026. You will lead a team of Learning & Development Partners. You are expected to engage and collaborate closely with our internal stakeholders to drive performance, growth and capability development. A key aspect of your role will be partnering with Divisions to conduct comprehensive training needs analysis, identifying skills gaps and learning requirements to develop targeted solutions that address their specific needs. These responsibilities include developing, implementing, and reviewing competency frameworks and training roadmaps, as well as designing and implementing L&D strategies, plans, and policies. You will collaborate with external stakeholders (MINDEF/SAF, Whole-of-Government (WoG) agencies, and commercial entities) to source, manage, and evaluate local and overseas training courses to ensure alignment with MSD’s L&D objectives and evolving training needs. You will also design, deliver and evaluate in-house course curricula, including managing training-related administrative processes and associated training resources effectively. As a Learning and Development (L&D) Partner, you will contribute across the full spectrum of learning capability development. Your key responsibilities include: • Develop, implement, and review L&D policies, competency frameworks, training plans, and roadmaps in close collaboration with internal stakeholders to support their long-term capability development. • Manage and review local and overseas training programmes to ensure they remain relevant, comply with governance standards, align with MSD’s organisational strategy and adapt to the changing workforce needs. • Coordinate and manage training operations, from budget planning and training providers management to participant enrolment and stakeholder engagement, while ensuring smooth logistical execution. • Design, deliver, and evaluate in-house training and curricula using varied instructional methods suited for adult learners across different skill levels. • Use feedback and evaluation data to assess training effectiveness and enhance both programme quality and outcomes. • Source, curate and collaborate with partners (e.g., MINDEF/SAF, Whole-of-Government, commercial providers) on their course delivery, training resources, and evaluation efforts. • Provide regular progress updates, key findings, and strategic recommendations to Management to inform L&D decisions and goals. Strong team player, effective written and verbal communication, and stakeholder management skills are essential. You should also have a good understanding of user-centric design and change management principles, as well as strong analytical and organisational abilities. The ability to think and take a systematic approach to implementing L&D policies and executing learning interventions in a timely manner is critical. Additionally, strong planning, coordination, and people management skills are important for executing training plans and managing courses effectively while optimising training resources. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment is key to success in this role.

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 4 Jun 2026. Closing on 09 Jun 2027. As Director (Assurance), you will serve as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to public agency leadership, leading high-performing internal audit teams delivering Shared IA Services to Ministries and Statutory Boards. This is not simply an audit leadership role — you will be a change agent, driving the evolution of IA practices across the public sector through digital innovation, agile methodologies, and a broadened risk lens that encompasses technology, cybersecurity, and sustainability. You will shape the future of the public sector IA community by building capabilities, professionalising practices, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and intellectual curiosity. Strategic Audit Leadership You will direct the planning, management, and execution of risk-based audit engagements across agencies under AGD's portfolio of clients, ensuring timely delivery and consistently high audit quality. Moving beyond traditional compliance-focused auditing, you will develop and maintain a forward-looking audit universe that reflects emerging risks and align audit priorities with the broader governance and risk landscape of the public sector. You will also champion agile auditing methodologies, designing shorter and more iterative audit cycles that deliver faster, more actionable insights to stakeholders. Digital Transformation You will lead the integration of data analytics, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI-assisted audit tools into the audit methodology to enable continuous monitoring and deeper audit insights. You will oversee the adoption of audit management platforms to improve workflow efficiency and documentation standards. Staying ahead of developments in generative AI, machine learning, and other emerging technologies, you will assess their applicability to the IA function and build the team's capacity to leverage these tools effectively. Experience with data analytics tools such as Power BI, or Python in an audit context will be particularly valued. Emerging Risk and Advisory As a strategic advisor, you will engage credibly with C-suite and senior public sector leadership, translating complex audit findings into clear, business-relevant insights that drive meaningful governance improvements. You will provide assurance and advisory perspectives on a broadened risk landscape, including IT general controls, cybersecurity risk, digital business processes, third-party and supply chain risk, and increasingly, sustainability and ESG governance frameworks. You will work closely with agency leadership to anticipate risks before they materialise, positioning IA as a forward-looking function rather than a retrospective one. Community Building and Capability Development You will work with IA heads across the public sector to build a vibrant community of practice, driving the development of shared frameworks, toolkits, and upskilling programmes that raise the overall standard of public sector IA. You will implement capability development roadmaps that equip IA practitioners with both technical audit competencies and digital skills — including data literacy, AI fluency, and agile ways of working. You will represent AGD in cross-agency forums and professional bodies to advance the ambition of public sector IA. People Leadership and Culture You will manage, mentor, and develop a team of IA professionals, building a pipeline of future audit leaders who are technically strong, digitally capable, and strategically minded. You will foster a team culture that values psychological safety, diversity of thought, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine commitment to public service excellence. Candidate will review systems infrastructure, design and architecture to ensure cybersecurity factors are considered and in compliance within existing government IM8 requirements. These systems are software intensive, complex and requires high availability. Depending on the phase of the systems lifecycle, candidate will be assigned to specify the technical requirements of the systems, evaluate on the proposed solutions, work on relevant approvals, execute the implementation of enhancement or technical refresh as well as maintenance of the systems. Responsibilities Key responsibilities include: Manage ANS projects/ systems including cyber-security implementations, as well as the design and engineering information security (e.g. authentication, perimeter security, security compliance tools), technology systems (software & hardware), and security policies / procedures. Implement solutions to enhance cyber-security posture (e.g. cyber defenses, mitigation measures) to meet CAAS’, national, international standards and requirements. Work closely with multiple stakeholders both internal and external (including other government agencies, system suppliers, maintenance operators, operation users, IT consultants/auditors etc) which include coordinate, liaise, support and conduct meetings to facilitate and validate the implementation in accordance with national and international cybersecurity standards and requirements. Coordinate, liaise, support and conduct internal as well as external audit needs/issues including technical discussions and internal audits (e.g. scanning exercises, penetration tests). Formulate process and procedures relating to cyber security through continuous engagement with the various stakeholders including the regulator, industry players and relevant agencies. Keep abreast of the latest industry cybersecurity practices and technologies as well as emerging threats and vulnerabilities, then recommend appropriate controls for implementation to improve the ANS systems security posture. Conduct investigations into security breaches to determine the cause of the incidents and work closely with multiple stakeholders both internal and external to resolve the incidents, participate in post-incident reporting and study/implement the proposed enhancement to the systems and infrastructure to close the security gaps. Manage relevant security documentation and updating of the ANS Group's overall security programme, including planning, coordinating and conducting relevant training for security and assurance matters to raise and maintain high cyber security awareness in the ANS Group. Coordinate internal and external audit needs/issues and participate in technical discussions and internal audit (e.g. scanning exercises, penetration tests). Trained in Cybersecurity, I

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 24 Jul 2026. Closing in 2 day(s). Singapore is internationally renowned for our transport infrastructure and for being a global aviation and maritime hub. We seek dynamic, analytical and committed individuals to join our able MOT team in realising our vision of a global interconnected transport hub. If you share our vision and possess the qualities we seek, do join us! Our air hub is of strategic and existential importance for Singapore. It supports economic links and people-to-people flows with the rest of the world, and catalyses growth opportunities for the Singapore economy. You will work closely with the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore and other Government agencies. Strong critical reasoning, with good analytical, numerical, and problem-solving skills. b. Excellent writing and communication. c. Good interpersonal skills, able to work well with diverse stakeholders with different interests, to drive collaboration, convergence and concrete outcomes. d. Comfortable with ambiguity, with a bias towards action, and a curiosity that drives learning. e. Good team player with a positive, can-do attitude.
